## 1. Purpose

This procedure describes the extraction and quantification of
water-extractable dissolved organic carbon (WEOC) from soil. WEOC
represents the fraction of soil organic matter that is readily
soluble in water and includes simple sugars, organic acids, amino
acids, and other low-molecular-weight compounds. It is a sensitive
indicator of labile carbon availability, microbial substrate supply,
and changes in soil management or land use [@ghani2003; @jones2006].

WEOC is distinct from the K~2~SO~4~-extractable DOC measured in the
chloroform fumigation-extraction method
([SOP-L409](SOP-L409-microbial-biomass-carbon.qmd)) and from total
soil organic carbon ([SOP-L407](SOP-L407-total-carbon.qmd)). The
water extraction uses no salt, making it a closer analogue to the
dissolved organic carbon that would leach from soil under natural
rainfall or irrigation.


## 2. Scope

- **Applies to:** Mineral and organic soil samples, compost, and
  organic amendments. Samples should be collected per
  [SOP-F400 Soil Sampling](../field_sops/SOP-F400-soil-sampling.qmd)
  and stored at 4 C (for field-moist analysis) or air-dried.
- **Does not apply to:** Water samples (analyze directly on the TOC-L),
  K~2~SO~4~ extracts for microbial biomass carbon (see SOP-L409), or
  total soil carbon by combustion (see SOP-L407)
- **Location:** EA Program laboratory, SGM 133


## 3. Responsibilities

| Role              | Responsibility                              |
|:------------------|:--------------------------------------------|
| Lab PI            | Approve SOP, ensure training compliance     |
| Trained Personnel | Perform extraction and submit samples for TOC analysis |
| New Students      | Complete training before independent use    |


## 4. Safety and Hazards

::: {.callout-warning}
### Hazards

- **Physical:** Drying oven (105 C) and orbital shaker pose minor
  physical hazards.
- **Biological:** Soil samples may harbor pathogens. Wash hands after
  handling soil.
- **Chemical:** Concentrated HCl (if used for acidification before
  TOC analysis) is corrosive.
:::

### Required PPE

- [ ] Safety glasses
- [ ] Lab coat
- [ ] Nitrile gloves

### Emergency Procedures

For acid splashes, flush with water for at least 15 minutes. Refer to
[SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd).


## 5. Equipment and Materials

### Equipment

| Item                                  | Location  | Notes                          |
|:--------------------------------------|:----------|:-------------------------------|
| Orbital or end-over-end shaker        | SGM 133   |                                |
| Centrifuge (capable of 4,000 x g)     | SGM 133   |                                |
| Vacuum filtration apparatus or syringe filters | SGM 133 |                         |
| Shimadzu TOC-L analyzer               | SGM 133   | See [SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd) |
| Analytical balance (0.01 g)           | SGM 133   | See [SOP-L200](SOP-L200-analytical-balance-calibration.qmd) |
| Drying oven (105 C)                   | SGM 133   | For gravimetric moisture       |

### Reagents and Consumables

| Item                                       | Notes                          |
|:-------------------------------------------|:-------------------------------|
| Deionized water (Type I or II, 18.2 MOhm)  | Carbon-free; verify with TOC blank |
| 50 mL centrifuge tubes (polypropylene)     | Pre-rinsed with DI water       |
| 0.45 um membrane or syringe filters        | Pre-combusted glass fiber (GF/F) or PVDF; do not use cellulose acetate (leaches DOC) |
| Pre-combusted 40 mL glass vials with PTFE-lined caps | For TOC-L analysis    |
| 2 M HCl                                   | For acidifying extracts if NPOC mode is used |


## 6. Procedure

### 6.1 Sample Preparation

1. If using field-moist soil, determine gravimetric moisture content on
   a separate subsample per [SOP-L400](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd)
2. If using air-dried soil, pass through a 2 mm sieve and determine
   residual moisture content

### 6.2 Extraction

1. Weigh 5.0 g (oven-dry equivalent) of soil into a 50 mL centrifuge
   tube. Record the exact mass.
2. Add 25 mL of deionized water (1:5 soil-to-water ratio)
   [@ghani2003; @jones2006]
3. Cap the tube and shake on an end-over-end or orbital shaker at
   approximately 150 rpm for 1 hour at room temperature
4. Centrifuge at 4,000 x g for 10 minutes to separate the supernatant

::: {.callout-tip}
Some protocols use a hot water extraction (80 C for 16 hours) to
capture a larger fraction of labile carbon [@ghani2003]. If hot water
extraction is desired, specify the temperature and duration explicitly
in the lab notebook and report, as the two methods are not directly
comparable.
:::

### 6.3 Filtration

1. Filter the supernatant through a 0.45 um filter into a pre-combusted
   glass vial
2. If using syringe filters, discard the first 2--3 mL of filtrate to
   flush any carbon leached from the filter
3. Collect at least 15 mL of filtrate for TOC analysis (enough for
   multiple injections plus rinse volume)

### 6.4 Storage

1. If extracts cannot be analyzed within 24 hours, acidify to pH less
   than 2 with 2 M HCl (approximately 1 drop per 10 mL) and store at
   4 C
2. Analyze within 7 days of extraction; prolonged storage may alter
   DOC concentrations even when acidified

### 6.5 DOC Analysis

1. Analyze filtered extracts on the Shimadzu TOC-L in NPOC mode per
   [SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd)
2. Prepare a deionized water blank and extraction blanks (DI water
   processed through the full extraction procedure) alongside samples
3. Run calibration standards (potassium hydrogen phthalate, KHP) as
   described in SOP-L204

### 6.6 Calculations

$$
\text{WEOC (mg C kg}^{-1}\text{ dry soil)} =
\frac{(C_{\text{sample}} - C_{\text{blank}}) \times V_{\text{extract}}}{m_{\text{soil}}}
$$

where:

- $C_{\text{sample}}$ = DOC concentration in the filtered extract
  (mg C/L)
- $C_{\text{blank}}$ = DOC concentration in the extraction blank
  (mg C/L)
- $V_{\text{extract}}$ = total volume of extractant added (L; e.g.,
  0.025 L)
- $m_{\text{soil}}$ = oven-dry mass of soil extracted (kg)


## 7. Quality Control and Acceptance Criteria

- Include extraction blanks (DI water only, no soil) in each batch to
  quantify background carbon from filters, tubes, and water
- Run sample duplicates for at least 10% of samples; CV between
  duplicates should be less than 10%
- Include a laboratory reference soil in each batch
- Verify that extraction blank DOC is less than 1 mg/L; if higher,
  troubleshoot water quality and filter blanks
- Instrument QC follows [SOP-L204](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd)
  requirements (calibration verification, instrument blanks, replicate
  injection CV less than 2%)


## 8. Waste Disposal

| Waste Type                    | Disposal Method                          |
|:------------------------------|:-----------------------------------------|
| Soil residue after extraction | Standard trash or return to sample stock |
| Filtered water extracts       | Drain with copious water (non-hazardous) |
| Acidified extracts            | Neutralize and drain, or collect for EH&S |
| Used filters                  | Standard trash                           |

## 10. Training Record

Before performing this procedure independently, personnel must:

1. Read this SOP in full
2. Complete [SOP-L002 Laboratory Safety](SOP-L002-laboratory-safety.qmd)
   training
3. Complete [SOP-L400 Soil Moisture](SOP-L400-soil-moisture.qmd)
   training (required for moisture correction)
4. Be trained on [SOP-L204 Shimadzu TOC-L](SOP-L204-shimadzu-toc-l.qmd)
   or have extracts analyzed by a trained operator
5. Perform the extraction under supervision with acceptable duplicate
   precision (CV less than 10%)
6. Be signed off by the PI or lab manager
